### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A32, A33 and A38 each ran in about 49 in 100 cases and always together (co-occurrence about 48 in 100); in the later window each appears in only about 1 in 200 cases (0.5%). [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL028, REL029, REL030, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- In the earlier window, A27 ran in about 52 in 100 cases (mean about 0.5 occurrences per trace); in the later window it runs in 199 of 200 cases with about one occurrence per trace. [OCC004]
- Routing out of A26 changed accordingly: before, about 50% of its outgoing transitions went to A27 and about 48% to A32, A33 or A38; in the later window about 98% go to A27. [DIR006]
- A27 now sits between A26 and A28: A26 precedes A27 in about 98.5 in 100 later cases (about 51 in 100 before), A27 precedes A28 in about 96.5 in 100 later cases (before, A28 usually ran without A27, about 48.5 in 100), and the A26→A28 distance is now 2 steps in about 95 in 100 cases versus an even split between 2 and 4 steps before. [REL017, REL021, LAG003]
- A04 dropped sharply: from about 68 in 100 cases (with about 90% of A04's outgoing transitions leading to A15) to about 21.5 in 100 cases; A14's outgoing flow moved from A04 (about 63% of transitions) to A15 (about 82%), and A14 reaches A15 within one step in about 47% of cases versus about 19% before. [OCC002, POS001, DIR004, DIR002, REL001, LAG001, LAG002]
- Minor: A02 and A08 became more frequent (about 5 in 100 cases before versus about 15 and 20.5 in 100 after) with largely new successor sets; these profiles rest on few observations. [OCC001, OCC003, DIR001, DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the branch composed of A32, A33 and A38 — previously executed together in roughly half of the cases and reached from A26 in about 48% of its outgoing transitions — is no longer executed, while A27, previously an alternative taken from A26 in about half the cases, now runs in virtually every case between A26 and A28 (A26 → A27 → A28). This is shown directly by directional and relational items with strong support in both windows (A26's outgoing profile rests on about 200 traces per window; the A26/A27 and A27/A28 relations on all 200 per window) and is consistent across occurrence, direction, relation and lag indicators, although several of these items describe the same traces and are not independent confirmations. With 62 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected by chance, the set as a whole cannot be explained by random sampling. The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the A32/A33/A38 branch still exists but has become extremely rare: it appears in 1 of 200 later traces, and its post-change routing rests on that single trace. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, DIR006, REL017, REL021, LAG003, REL028, REL029, REL030]

Other differences: A04 was largely dropped from the flow between A14 and A15 — before, A14 led to A04 in about 63% of its transitions and A04 led to A15 in about 90% of its own; in the later window A14 leads directly to A15 (about 82% of its transitions) and A04 appears in only about 21.5 in 100 cases — a second path replacement at a different location that the evidence does not link to the A26/A27 restructuring; A02 and A08 also became more frequent. [OCC002, POS001, DIR004, DIR002, REL001, LAG001, LAG002, OCC001, OCC003, DIR001, DIR003]
